EXHIBITION BOOK READER — how to use
===================================

What it does
  Reads photos of the China Import and Export Fair exhibitor catalog pages and
  saves every exhibitor (booth, Chinese/English name, address, postcode, tel,
  fax, e-mail, website, category, page) into an Excel file.
  Everything runs on your laptop. No internet and no installation needed.

Needs
  Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. About 300 MB of free disk space.

Steps
  1. Put ExhibitionBookReader.exe anywhere (Desktop or Documents is fine).
  2. Double-click it. The first start takes 5-10 seconds (a small
     "Exhibition Book Reader" splash shows while it unpacks).
  3. "Photos folder" -> Browse... -> choose the folder with the page photos
     (.jpg / .jpeg / .png). The window shows how many photos it found.
     Tip: if the exe sits in the same folder as the photos, it is already chosen.
  4. "Save to" is filled in for you (an "output" folder inside the photos folder).
  5. Press Start (or F5). It takes about 25 seconds per photo.
     Press Stop (or Esc) to stop after the current photo.
  6. When it is done, press "Open Excel file".

Taking good photos
  - One page per photo, the whole page in the frame, upright, in focus.
  - Good, even light; avoid strong shadows across the text.
  - Name the files so they sort in page order (the camera's date/time names do).
    A company whose details continue on the next page is joined automatically
    only when the pages are read in order.

Checking the results
  - Click a row to see all its fields and the exact text that was read.
  - Rows highlighted in yellow need a second look (something is missing or the
    text was hard to read). "Needs review only" shows just those rows.
  - OCR is good but not perfect: a letter can occasionally be wrong in a name.

If Windows warns you
  - "Windows protected your PC" (SmartScreen): click "More info" -> "Run anyway".
    The program is not signed by a publisher, that is all the warning means.
  - If an antivirus quarantines it, restore it / allow it. Programs packed this
    way are sometimes flagged by mistake.

Access (.accdb) output
  Only available when Microsoft Access (or the free "Microsoft Access Database
  Engine", 64-bit) is installed. Otherwise the Access box is greyed out and
  only the Excel file is written — the Excel file has the same data.
